title: Civil Rights Movement (United States)
summary: The United States civil rights movement challenged legal racial segregation and discrimination in the 1950s and 1960s. The Supreme Court's unanimous Brown v. Board of Education decision of 17 May 1954 against segregated public schools served as a catalyst. Federal laws followed: the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Voting Rights Act of 1965 and the Fair Housing Act of 1968.

uncertainty.note: The ADL dates the civil rights legislation 1954-1968; the National Park Service dates the modern movement 1954-1964.

as_recorded.value: Civil rights legislation was passed between 1954 and 1968
